surface: Display / seed-exfiltration side channels (key=display): seed-wizard word display + recovery entry, PIN row, legacy 16x4 glyph blitter, ui-px pixel presenter, NV3007 SPI1 bus (pq1 PA4/PA5/PA7, write-only, no MISO), backlight, consumption mask, framebuffer residue, display-bus implant detection, and backup flows. Gap analysis against HEAD c75b0d9c of feat/pq1-board-target, read-only; Trezor @ 6ab39e95cf re-read for precedents. Headline: the only confirmed in-the-wild hardware-wallet implant (Ledger Nano X, 2025-26) passively sniffed the already-SE-driven display SPI and template-matched glyphs — so 'SE-driven display' is not the lever; the levers are (a) make the secret glyph stream useless to a fixed-template tap and content-independent on the bus, (b) detect added bus load / added power draw before the wizard runs, (c) close the two remaining non-constant-time secret-glyph windows the repo still has, and (d) stop pixel-form residue outliving the wizard.

improvements.title: Route the PIN active digit and the restore-wizard letter row through the constant-time secret glyph path on a forced frame, and pin it with a regression test
improvements.threat: EM/power probe on the NV3007 SPI stream or on the MCU during PIN entry / seed restore. Each PIN commit screen paints exactly one secret digit at a known cell through the address-keyed public font (legacy) or the non-forced Item::Text run (px, strip-digest skip + 64-bit digest of secret pixels left in `static mut SHOWN`); eight screens = the PIN. The restore wizard letter row leaks every typed seed letter the same way (#784). This is the same channel F-24/F-27 closed for the word pages — TVLA on the legacy scan measured 650.90 leaky vs 0.00 CT.
improvements.proposal: (1) Legacy: in `pin_entry::render_pin_screen` and `seed_wizard::render_letter_screen` build the secret row via `secret_text::secret_glyph_cols` and emit it with `flush_with_secret_rows` instead of `draw_line`+`flush`. (2) px: make `status_map::pin_row` / `letter_row` emit the active digit / typed letters as `Item::Secret` cells (placeholders in the record, bytes passed as `secret`) and call `screens::show_with(&row, &secret)` so `play_screen` sets `force = true` (present_frame_ex streams every strip, records no digest, invalidates SHOWN). Extend `Font::blit_secret_run`'s candidate range from a-z to a-z + 0-9 (or a second numeric run) for the digit. (3) Add the host test #784 recommends: every Screen produced by pin_row/letter_row/seed_page/candidate_list that carries a secret is presented with a non-empty `secret` (force=true) and never through `show()`. (4) Also re-randomise the start digit of the NEXT position after each accepted digit (Trezor caesar `set_page_counter(get_random_digit_position())`), not once per session.
improvements.rationale: Cheapest, highest-certainty fix on the surface: the CT primitives, the forced-frame discipline and the host-test scaffolding already exist; only two call sites and one builder still bypass them. The PIN is the key to the device and the restore letters are the seed itself — both are strictly more valuable than the word pages that are already protected.

improvements.title: Display-bus implant self-check: factory-enrolled electrical fingerprint of SPI1/DC lines (GPIO RC-decay timing), re-verified at boot and immediately before the seed wizard / PIN entry
improvements.threat: Supply-chain / reseller-stage hardware implant tapping the NV3007 SPI (SCK/MOSI/CS/DC) to capture seed words and PIN glyphs — exactly the Ledger Nano X implant class (passive SPI sniff + glyph template match + LTE exfil). pq1 has no detection at all: the firmware is genuine, the board is not, and the only documented layer is photos + packaging (user-device-verification.md:163-168).
improvements.proposal: Firmware self-test on the four trusted-display lines, run with the panel idle and CS deasserted: for each line, configure the pin as open-drain output with the internal pull-up (NOT analog mode — see the #705 IDR lesson), drive low, release, and count DWT cycles until IDR reads high; repeat N times with the mask PWM paused. The decay constant is pull-up R (~40 k) x total line capacitance (trace + panel input + any tap). An implant input pin plus its stub adds roughly 3-10 pF on a ~15-30 pF net, i.e. a 10-50% shift, resolvable at 160 MHz. Make it ratiometric (each line vs the others, which share process corner and temperature) and temperature-compensated via the internal temperature sensor ADC. Enrol the per-line baseline band at the factory (RDP-0 stage, written to a per-device page or OTP) and re-check at every boot and immediately before `show_mnemonic`, `enter_pin`, and the restore wizard; a miss refuses the wizard/sign with a loud trusted-UI screen and advises the verification ceremony. Treat this as the pq1 analogue of PACTOR's sub-pF capacitance sensing with the temperature-selected threshold their v2 needed.
improvements.rationale: The one real implant sat on the display bus, the user's direct question is 'can the FSBL or similar detect malicious hardware', and no vendor ships anything. pq1 is unusually well placed: the secure image owns SPI1 and its GPIOs (GTZC-secured), the bus is short (PA4/PA5/PA7 under the same port), and the factory already does a per-device OTP/flash ceremony at RDP-0 where a baseline can be recorded, so a reseller-stage implant (the CryptoBilis pattern) is inserted AFTER enrolment and IS catchable. A self-enrolled first-field-boot baseline would not be (deep-research digest) — hence factory enrolment.

improvements.title: Power-budget attestation: VBUS/3V3 shunt + ADC current sense read at boot idle and during the seed wizard, against a design-derived band
improvements.threat: Active implant (LTE/BLE modem + MCU) powered from the device. pq1 has no battery (owner decision), so an exfiltrating implant must either draw from USB VBUS/3V3 or carry its own cell inside an enclosure with no battery cavity. An LTE Cat.1 modem draws tens of mA idle and hundreds of mA on TX; a Cortex-M0+ sniffer draws single-digit mA — all far above the ~1 mW resolution the Piliposyan detector achieves, and the Ledger implant had to spoof battery telemetry precisely because it was power-visible.
improvements.proposal: EVT board change: a low-side or high-side shunt (e.g. 50-100 mOhm) on the VBUS->3V3 regulator INPUT (upstream of every rail an implant could tap, including the SE rail switches LDO2_EN/SE1_EN and LCM_EN), read by a U585 ADC channel on one of the free bonded pins (PA10 or PA6 if the mask moves). Firmware: at boot with all peripherals in a known state (SEs off via rail switches, backlight at a fixed brightness, mask off) read the quiescent current; compare against a design-derived band from the BOM + factory-measured per-unit value (recorded at the RDP-0 ceremony); re-read during the seed wizard (radio TX bursts are the loudest moment). Out-of-band → refuse wizard/sign with a loud screen. Pair with D-02: capacitance catches passive taps, current catches active ones.
improvements.rationale: No battery is a structural advantage over Ledger/Trezor T3W1: the implant's energy must come through one measurable choke point. The attacker's demonstrated counter (telemetry spoofing) is only possible when the sense element is downstream of or inside the tampered subassembly; a shunt at the USB input on the main PCB forces them to modify the main board itself, which the SWD/RDP-0 verification + photo ceremony already covers.

improvements.title: Content-independent SPI payload for secret cells: equal-Hamming-weight / equal-transition RGB565 colour pair for secret glyphs (bus-level constant-weight encoding)
improvements.threat: EM / crosstalk / supply leakage of the 20 MHz MOSI stream (and the panel source-driver current) during seed, candidate-list, letter-row and PIN frames. Today the glyph FETCH is constant-time but the PAYLOAD is maximal-contrast 0xFFFF/0x0000: every secret pixel toggles all 16 bits, so the per-pixel Hamming weight and transition count on the bus is exactly the glyph bitmap (Kuhn's FPD-link TEMPEST / Screen Gleaning class, averaged across the periodic refresh).
improvements.proposal: For secret rows/cells only (legacy `blit_glyph` FG/BG and px `Item::Secret` via `blend_ct`), replace the colour pair with a pair (fg, bg) chosen by brute-force search over RGB565 such that: equal Hamming weight, equal intra-word transition count, equal first and last bit (so inter-pixel boundary transitions are also glyph-independent), and acceptable luminance contrast on the NV3007 (verify on glass). Quantise px anti-aliased coverage for secret cells to the two-colour pair (or to a small set of pairs that all satisfy the constraints) so no intermediate colour leaks. Optionally surround the secret cell band with a constant lit field (Trezor legacy inversion) so the panel's row current is dominated by a content-independent background. Keep this orthogonal to the glyph-fetch CT path and to the atlas pin (colour is applied in the compositor, not the atlas).
improvements.rationale: This is the SPI-panel translation of Trezor's `oledSCA` constant-weight rows and Ledger's inverted PIN boxes: make the electrical signature per secret pixel independent of the bit. On a 3-wire SPI TFT the bus bits ARE the leak carrier, so weight/transition equalisation attacks the channel at its source with a two-constant change on the legacy path and a small compositor change on px. It does nothing against a logic-level tap (D-02/D-03/D-05 cover that) and that must be stated.

improvements.title: Defeat fixed-template glyph taps and shrink the exposure window: per-session randomised glyph geometry/colour-LSB jitter, one-word-at-a-time reveal with random hold, dimmed wizard backlight, and the 'never put your backup anywhere digital' screen
improvements.threat: A passive display-bus tap with an on-implant glyph template matcher (the Ledger implant stored a-z templates at 0x4D00-0x4E40 and matched the SPI stream), plus camera/EM averaging across a periodic refresh (Kuhn: a cached, pixel-identical glyph 'merely assists the eavesdropper'), plus the no-countermeasure photo/shoulder residual.
improvements.proposal: (a) In the compositor (after atlas verification, so the SHA-256 pin is untouched), apply a per-session TRNG-chosen sub-cell x/y offset per secret cell, randomised low-order colour bits (within D-04's weight constraints), and if the atlas budget allows, K glyph variants per letter chosen per cell; this makes a byte-exact template matcher miss and forces the implant to carry an OCR, raising its size/power (which D-03 then sees). (b) Offer a one-word-per-page mode (24 frames, each word with its index) with a random 0-300 ms pre-display hold so no single leaked frame carries more than one word and frame boundaries are not USB/host-alignable; keep scroll-to-end. (c) pq1: program the AW99703 to a low brightness during the wizard (REG_LEDMSB/LSB are already written once at init) to cut backlight-rail and driver emission amplitude. (d) Add Trezor's pre-display warning page.
improvements.rationale: The implant that actually existed was a fixed-template matcher; cheap per-session rendering diversity is the one software measure that targets it directly, and it is the countermeasure Kuhn identified as the only effective software one against FPD-link TEMPEST. Fewer words per frame and a dimmer, jittered reveal cut both electrical and optical exposure per frame at near-zero cost, and avoid the decoy-frame approach that failed on glass twice (#258).

improvements.title: Consumption mask parity: re-randomise on every display flush, DMA-fed TRNG duty table on a secure GPDMA channel, and put an actual load on the mask pin
improvements.threat: Trace alignment on frame transmission: the attacker aligns a power/EM trace on the SPI frame (the moment content-dependent current/EM appears). pq1's mask is re-randomised only from the secure tick, from a xorshift PRNG, and drives an NC pad, so it neither decorrelates per frame nor demonstrably dilutes anything.
improvements.proposal: (1) Call `hw::consumption_mask::randomize()` at the top of `lcd::Display::flush` / `flush_with_secret_rows` and in `px::lcd::present_frame_ex` before the first strip goes out (Trezor's `display_refresh` hook), drawing that sample from rng_strong rather than the xorshift. (2) Port Trezor's DMA-fed table: a 119-entry duty table in S-SRAM refreshed from the TRNG, GPDMA1 channel in circular linked-list mode triggered by TIMx_UP writing CCR1 every 100 us, with the channel configured SEC|PRIV|SRC_SEC|DEST_SEC so NS cannot halt it (the module header already lists this as the follow-up). (3) EVT: route the mask pin (pq1 PA6, currently NC) to a small resistive load across the 3V3 near the die so the duty cycle actually modulates supply current; then measure dilution with the SCA bench (TVLA before/after) and close the 'unmeasured' caveat.
improvements.rationale: Direct Trezor parity on the same MCU family; (1) is a two-line change, (3) is the only thing that makes the production-mandatory fence mean something. Without (3) the feature is satisfied-by-construction, as CLAUDE.md admits.

improvements.title: Zeroize pixel-form secret residue and clear the panel GRAM/backlight on every lock, wipe and idle-timeout
improvements.threat: Post-lock SRAM dump, a later NS-reachable secure-world bug, or a powered-but-locked device whose TFT GRAM still holds the last wizard frame: the legacy `Display::cell` (720 B), the px `STRIP` static (13,696 B), `secret_rows_storage`/`wb` in the legacy mnemonic/candidate renderers, and the NV3007 GRAM all retain the last secret glyphs in pixel form after the wizard; `CMD_LOCK` only paints 'Locked'.
improvements.proposal: (1) Zeroize `cell` after each secret glyph blit and `STRIP` at the end of every forced frame (and at `invalidate_shown`), and zeroize `secret_rows_storage`/`wb` in `render_mnemonic_page` / legacy `render_candidate_screen` (the px twins already do). (2) On `cmd_lock`, idle-timeout wipe, tamper wipe and wizard exit: `fill_screen(BG)` the whole GRAM (not just the 16x4 text window), then de-assert LCM_EN / set AW99703 brightness 0 on pq1 and, where drivable, pulse the panel reset so GRAM is cleared in hardware. (3) Add a host test that the row/cell/strip buffers are all-zero after a forced frame completes.
improvements.rationale: Trezor clears both physical framebuffers on display init and gates FB access by MPU; pq1 keeps everything in S-SRAM (stronger) but never erases it. Residue in pixel form is a seed-recovery oracle for any future bug, and the GRAM case is a physical one (a locked device on a desk still holds the frame until overwritten).

improvements.title: SE-keyed anti-phishing words at PIN entry (Coldcard / Passport 'Security Words'): detect a swapped or cloned device before the full PIN is typed
improvements.threat: Evil-maid / reseller swap: a look-alike device (or an implanted one with its own firmware) harvests the PIN as the user types it on the trusted UI; the boot fingerprint proves the firmware, not that this is the user's own unit, and a device with the same firmware shows the same 8 words.
improvements.proposal: After the first 4 PIN digits, compute inside an SE (SE050 HMAC over the prefix with a per-device SE-resident secret, or OPTIGA CMAC via a protected object, rate-limited by SE policy to ~2 s per distinct prefix) and render two BIP-39 words via the CT secret path; the user learns them at setup (shown once, written next to the device) and aborts PIN entry if they differ. Opt-in (Passport default-off) or default-on with an explicit setup step. Keep PIN comparison itself in SE silicon (invariant #2 untouched; the prefix MAC is a separate keyed object, never the PIN object).
improvements.rationale: Zero hardware cost, directly addresses the user's 'malicious hardware' question for the swap case (a clone cannot reproduce the SE-keyed words), and complements the FSBL fingerprint which only answers 'which firmware'.
repo_evidence: secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:8-30 (F-20 only; no device-authenticity words); grep anti-phish/security words/prefix in pin_entry.rs, cmd_request_unlock.rs, threat-model.md, trezor-comparison.md: none
secure/src/ui/secret_text.rs:73-82 (CT secret row primitive available to render the words)
improvements.vendor_precedent: Coldcard Mk4 anti-phishing words (HMAC over hashed PIN prefix in SE1, 2 s rate limit); Foundation Passport Prime 'Security Words' (off by default).
improvements.risks: Exposes a rate-limited 4-digit-prefix oracle on the SE (10,000 prefixes; with 2 s/attempt ~5.5 h to enumerate, which reveals the PIN prefix only if the user's words are known — the words are secret to the user, so the oracle yields nothing to an attacker without them). The words themselves become a secret displayed every unlock — must go through the CT/forced path (D-01) and the constant-weight pair (D-04). Needs an SE050 object/policy design and an attempt-counter interaction review so it cannot consume page-124/E120 budget.

improvements.title: Evidence and drift closure for the display surface: ui-px SCA harness for blit_secret_run, forced-frame/CT regression tests, threat-model §7.10 row, playbook rows, redact ui-capture, and fix the stale decoy/README/comment claims
improvements.threat: Silent regression: the px secret run's black_box barriers have the same LLVM-fold failure mode the legacy scan documents, and nothing measures it; stale docs claim gates that do not exist (font.rs:270 defers to a harness that only covers the legacy FONT_5X8 scan), so a future reviewer banks a false 'covered'.
improvements.proposal: (1) Add pqsigner-ui-px as a dependency of tools/sca/kdf_target and a `make -C tools/sca px-glyph-leak` TVLA (rainbow+lascar, mem_address + Hamming models) over `Font::blit_secret_run` with a leaky-baseline sentinel, run in CI like glyph-leak. (2) Kani/proptest over Item::Secret: pixel count and write pattern independent of the secret bytes. (3) Host tests: every secret-carrying Screen is presented forced (D-01) and scratch buffers are zero after a forced frame (D-07). (4) Redact seed rows in `semihosting::flush` before hashing (#186) instead of relying on the denylist. (5) Docs: add the §7.10 display-emanation row and trusted-UI/sca-fi playbook rows (bus EM, SPI timing, framebuffer residue, implant tap); correct tools/sca/README.md:1339-1400 (deleted `render_secret_row`/oled.rs references; decoy 'path forward' vs the recorded 20 MHz failure), seed_wizard.rs:315-320/1089-1096 stale predictions, px/screens.rs:14-17 'secrets never enter a record' (PIN digit/letters do), and refresh #237/#260 bodies from SSD1306 to NV3007 (single-LED AW99703, 20 mA full scale).
improvements.rationale: Every 'implemented' row on the px seed path is code-read evidence only; the project's own memory records that green runs with the path compiled out are not evidence. This item converts structural claims into measured ones and stops the documented drift from re-propagating.
